questions.question: Chemical formula of washing soda ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na₂CO₃.10H₂O.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 **Na2CO3.10H2O** is the chemical formula for** washing soda.**
 
 
• 
 It is a** sodium carbonate inorganic hydrate.**
 
 
• 
 As a result of its **extraction **from **plants **growing in sodium-rich soils, it was given the moniker soda ash.
 
 
• 
 It is a **metal carbonate **that is a white, crystalline solid and soluble in water.
 
 
• 
 Here are the **procedures **involved in producing sodium carbonate:

 
 
• 
 **Brine purification.**
 
 
• 
 **Sodium hydrogen carbonate production.**
 
 
• 
 **Creation of sodium carbonate.**
 
 
• 
 **Ammonia recovery.**
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Washing soda **applications**:

 
 
• Used in homes and businesses as **cleaning agent**.
 
• The **paper **industries ,**textile **industries ,**soap **industries ,and **detergent **industries all use it.
 
• It is a **component **of **water softening **process.
 
• It is employed in **production **of **glass**.
 
• One of the most **crucial agents **in laundries is washing soda.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of National Income?

options.text: It is always expressed with reference to the financial year.
It is included only in intermediate goods.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is included only in intermediate goods.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The following are the main **characteristics **of national income:

 
 
• 
 **Macroeconomic concepts **include national income.
 
 
• 
 Taking into account the **monetary value **of goods and services is national income.
 
 
• 
 An **extended period **of **time **is used to **measure **national income.
 
 
• 
 Considerations for national income include the net **total values **of products and services.
 
 
• 
 National income solely takes into account the value of final items to prevent **double counting**.
 
 
 
 
• 
 When calculating national income, the value of **intermediate items **is not taken into account.
 
 
• 
 **Net factor income **from **abroad **is **included **in national income (NFIA).
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• In the simplest terms, national income refers to a **country's riches.**
 
• The value of the commodities and services generated in an economy serves as a gauge of its **prosperity**.
 
• It represents the overall **monetary **worth of the commodities and services that a country produces in the course of a **fiscal year**.
 
• **Rent, wages, profits, **and **interests** are a few examples of payments that can be paid to different kinds of resources.
 
• The idea of national income is under the ambit of **macroeconomics**.

questions.question: According to census 2011, the child sex ratio was ______ females per 1000 males.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**919.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **ratio **of **females **to **men **in the **0–6 age group **is known as the child sex ratio.
 
• India's child sex ratio was **927 **in the census of **2001 **but dropped to **919 **in the census of **2011**.
 
• According to the **2011 Census**, **Haryana **has the **lowest child sex** **ratio **(834 per thousand men), while **Arunachal Pradesh**** **has the **highest **(971 females against 1000 males) among the Indian states.
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands **has the **greatest child sex ratio **of any Indian Union Territory, at 968 per 1,000 men.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The child sex ratio has **decreased **in India for a variety of causes.
 
• The society's desire for a **boy child over **a **girl child **is one of the **primary causes **of this threat.
 
• Sons will take** care of parents** in old age, extravagant **dowry **demands, men are the **breadwinners**, sons can **administer **the last rites and can take care of the parents, etc. are some other reasons.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer Yamini Krishnamurthy was awarded which of the following awards in 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Vibhushan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The** "Yamini school of Dance"** was established by **Yamini Krishnamurthy **in Delhi in **1990.**
 
• She has also produced a unique dancing programme for the **Doordarshan channel.**
 
• The critics gave her book **"A Passion for Dance"** positive reviews.
 
• Throughout her dance career, she received numerous honours, including the **Padma Shree (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001), and Padma Vibhushan (2016), **two of the highest civilian awards given out by the Indian Republic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• One of India's **first classical dancers **was Yamini Krishnamurthy.
 
• She has received training in both **Kuchipudi **and **Bharatanatyam**, two contrasting dancing styles.
 
• She was born in **Madanapalle**, Andhra Pradesh, on** December 20, 1940.**
 
• At** Chennai's Kalakshetra School of Dance, **Yamini Krishnamurthy studied **Bharatnatyam under Rukmini Devi Arundale. **
 
• Later, she received training from illustrious teachers like **Thanjavur Kittappa Pillai **and **Kanchipuram Ellappa Pillai.**
 
• Under the instruction of **Vedantam Lakshmi Narayana Shastri, Chinta Krishnamurthy, **and **Pasumarthy Venugopal Krishna Sharma, **she learned **Kuchipudi**.

questions.question: According to the archaeologists, in Harappan cities the part to the west was smaller and higher, was known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is C__**itadel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Numerous of these cities had two or more **distinct portions**.
 
• The area to the west was often **taller **and **smaller**.
 
• This is referred to by **archaeologists **as the **citadel**.
 
• In general, the **eastern portion **was **lower **and **larger**.
 
• The **lower town** is what it's known as.
 
• Each component was frequently surrounded by the **walls **made of **baked brick**.
 
• The bricks have **endured **for countless years because of how well they were built.
 
• The walls were **robust **because the bricks were arranged in an **interlocking manner**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Special buildings were built on the **citadel **in **certain cities**.
 
• For instance, in **Mohenjodaro**, a highly unusual tank known as the **Great Bath **was constructed in this region.
 
• This was plastered, lined with bricks, and sealed with a layer of natural tar to **prevent leaks**.
 
• From two sides, steps led down to it, and **chambers **surrounded it on all sides.
 
• Most likely, water was brought in from a **well **and emptied after usage.

questions.question: In November 2022, retired Army officer Raj Shukla has been appointed as a member of the _______.

__
 
• **Raj Shukla, **a **retired Army officer**, has been appointed to the** Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).**
 
• The** Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), Indian Police Service (IPS),** and **Central Services - Group A and Group B **are among the positions for which the UPSC recommends candidates to the government.
 
• On** Republic Day 2021**, Shukla received the** Param Vishisht Seva Medal** in honour of his service of the highest degree.
 
• Shukla, a skilled pilot and charismatic speaker, has written around **70 papers **and **publications **and delivered more than 180 lectures and seminars both in India and abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

• His **retirement **date was** March 31, 2022. **
 
• Shukla has held visiting **fellowships **at both the Centre for Land Warfare Studies and the Institute for Defense Studies and Analyses.

questions.question: In June 2022, the Supreme Court directed that every protected forest, national park and wildlife sanctuary across the country should have a mandatory eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) of a minimum ______ starting from their demarcated boundaries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 km.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court **mandated **an **eco-sensitive zone** of at least **one kilometre **starting from each **national park **and **wildlife sanctuary **in the country in an order that was published on **June 3, 2022**.
 
• The decision was taken in **response **to a **petition **to **protect forested regions **in **Tamil Nadu's Nilgiris district.**
 
• This decision **nullifies **the **ESZ border limit **around protected areas, as the Supreme Court previously declared.
 
• **All states** and **Union Territories **where the minimum ESZ extent is not stated would also be subject to it.
 
• Due to ideological differences between the **federal **and **state administrations** as well as between the states and their respective states, India does not have a statute that mandates the maintenance of the **eco-sensitive zone** surrounding its protected area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs) **and **Ecologically Fragile Areas (EFAs)** are related words (EFAs).
 
• The **MoEFCC** declares regions close to national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and protected areas as eco-sensitive zones.
 
• ESZs act as a kind of **"shock absorber" **for protected areas by regulating and monitoring activity inside and outside of them.
 
• The** National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)** asserts that any limitations should only be required when absolutely necessary and that the creation of eco-sensitive zones must be site-specific.

questions.question: What happens to the decomposition rate when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** It is slower.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The following **variables influence **the rate of decomposition:

 
 
• 
 **Chemical **make-up of detritus,
 
 
• 
 **pH**,
 
 
• 
 **Temperature**,
 
 
• 
 **Moisture, **and
 
 
• 
 **Aeration **of the **soil**.
 
 
 
 
• 
 Decomposition **proceeds **more **quickly **when the soil is **rich **in **nitrogen**.
 
 
• 
 The rate of decomposition is **accelerated **by the presence of **water**-**soluble carbohydrates**.
 
 
• 
 The degradation process is **slowed **down by the presence of big complex polymers in the debris, like** lignin and chitin.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The **breakdown** of **dead organic **matter into more **fundamental organic **or **inorganic **components including carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars, and mineral salts is known as decomposition, also referred to as rot.
 
• The process, which is a part of the **nutrient cycle**, is essential for recycling the scant material that occupies space in the biosphere.
 
• When a living organism passes away, the body begins to **decompose**.
 
• **Animals **like worms also contribute to the **breakdown **of the **chemical molecules**.
 
• Organisms that carry out this process are known as **decomposers **or **detritivores**.

questions.question: Rani Karnaa Nayak, who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2014, was a ______ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Many people consider **Rani Karnaa**, an Indian classical dancer famed for her mastery of the **Kathak **dance style, to be one of the genre's best practitioners.
 
• In **2014**, the Indian government recognised her contributions to the dance world by giving her the **Padma Shri**, the country's fourth-highest civilian honour.
 
• Rani Karnaa is credited with **fusing **the **customs **of the **Jaipur **and **Lucknow gharanas **in addition to spreading Kathak through her performances.
 
• Many commentators have praised her for her work fusing the **literature**, **music**, and **dance **of various cultural traditions with Kathak.
 
• She is credited with **fusing artistic expression **with **inventive thinking**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Rani Karnaa was born in **Hyderabad**, in what is now modern Pakistan and former British India, in **1939 **to a Sindhi dynasty of amirs.
 
• **Assandas Karnaa**, her father, was originally from the Karnamalani family in the **Larkana district**.
 
• Over time, the family name **Karnamalani **became shortened to Karanani and then to Karnaa.
 
• When Rani was three years old, her family **relocated **to **Delhi**.
 
• Her early education was in Delhi, and she received her degree in **botany **from the **Hindu College **there.
 
• Later, she earned an **Honours degree **in **Botany**, but she chose to focus on her **dance profession **rather than her academics.

questions.question: Black Card given to a badminton player during the game indicates _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**disqualification**.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Badminton**

 
 
• **​**__**Lawn, court, or badminton** game played with a** shuttlecock and lightweight rackets.**
 
• The shuttlecock, commonly referred to as a **"bird" or "birdie," **was historically a little cork hemisphere with 16 goose feathers sewn on it that weighed about 0.17 ounces (5 grams).
 
• Modern play may still employ these shuttles, although the Badminton World Federation also permits the use of synthetic shuttles.
 
• The game is called after Badminton,** which was initially played around **1873** at the duke of Beaufort's country home in Gloucestershire, England.**
 
• Poona, a game played by British army officers stationed in India in the 1860s, is directly related to badminton.
 
• **In 1899,** the first unofficial all-England men's badminton championships and the inaugural badminton competition for women were arranged the next year.
 
• **Badminton made its Olympic debut** in **1972 **as a demonstration sport and in 1988 as an exhibition sport. It was made a full-medal Olympic sport for the 1992 Games, including competition in the men's and women's singles (one against one) and doubles events (two against two). The mixed pairs event debuted in the 1996 Olympics.
 
• **As per the guidelines laid down by the Badminton World Federation (BWF),** the **length **of a standard badminton court remains the same - 13.40m (44 feet) - for both types of competitions. 
 
• But **the width differs** with the singles court running wide till 5.18m (17 feet), denoted by the side lines, while for the doubles court, the width is extended to 6.1m (20 feet), marked as the doubles sidelines. 
 
• The **2022 BWF World Championships were a badminton competition that took place from August 22 to August 28 at Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium in Tokyo, Japan** (formally known as the Total Energies BWF World Championships 2022 due to sponsorship considerations).

questions.question: Who has been appointed as NITI Aayog's new Vice Chairman in May 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suman Bery.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** NITI Aayog **__

 __
 
• ​​The NITI Aayog has taken the place of the **Planning Commission**, which has a legacy dating back **65 years. **For a longer time, the Planning Commission's usefulness and importance had been questioned. The alternative appears to be more appropriate and sensitive to the nation's current economic needs.
 
• **NITI Aayog Chairman – **Narendra Modi
 
• **NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman** – Shri Suman Bery is currently Vice Chairperson, NITI Aayog, in the rank and status of a Cabinet Minister. An experienced policy economist and research administrator, Mr Bery took over as NITI Aayog Vice Chairperson from 1 May 2022.
 
• **NITI Aayog Revolution**

 Aayog was established on **January 1st, 2015.** The word "NITI" signifies **morals, behaviour, instruction,** etc. in Sanskrit. However, it refers to policy in the current context, and NITI stands for **"National Institution for Transforming India.**" It is the leading institution for formulating national policy and is anticipated to support the nation's economic expansion. It aspires to build a powerful state that will aid in building a vibrant and powerful country. This aids India's emergence as a significant global economy. Both the **"Team India Hub" and the "Knowledge and Innovation Hub"** are projects of the NITI Aayog.

 __
 
• **​**__​​​__​__Pro-people: it fulfils the aspirations of society as well as individuals

• Pro-activity: in anticipation of and response to citizen needs
 
• Participation: involvement of the citizenry
 
• Empowering: Empowering, especially women in all aspects
 
• Inclusion of all: inclusion of all people irrespective of caste, creed, and gender
 
• Equality: Providing equal opportunity to all especially for youth
 
• Transparency: Making the government visible and responsive.

questions.question: Who among the following is said to have devised many Raagas or melodies in Hindustani music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tansen.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Tansen **__

 __
 
• **Birth year: 1506​__**
 
• **Birthplace: Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh**
 
• **Name at birth: Ramtanu**
 
• **1586 is the death year.**
 
• **Death Place: Agra**
 
• **Vocalist, composer of music, and instrumentalist**
 
• Husseini is his spouse
 
• Hamirsen, Suratsen, Tanras Khan, Saraswati Devi, and Bilas Khan are among the kids.
 
• Mukund Mishra is the father.
 
• **Awards: Akbar bestowed upon him the title of "Miyan."**
 
• Tansen, regarded as India's best musician, is credited with inventing the classical music that predominates in the country's northern regions (Hindustani classical music). Tansen was a vocalist and musician who wrote a lot of ragas. He began as King Ram Chand of Rewa State's court singer. According to legend, after learning of his amazing musical abilities, Emperor Akbar transformed him into his own musician. He afterwards became one of the** Navaratnas (Nine Gems) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. **The life of Tansen is associated with many legends. Some of the most common ones are his ability to create rain and fire by just using his musical skills. Whatever the legends may be, there is no denying the fact that he was the greatest among all musicians this country has ever produced.
 
 
 
• __**Tansen's Connection with Miracles**__
 __
 
• According to legend, the renowned singer was capable of working many miracles through his voice. According to a well-known narrative, Akbar's ministers came up with a scheme when they wanted to purposefully embarrass Tansen. The emperor was contacted by the ministers, who begged him to persuade Tansen to sing the **Raga Deepak**,** a raga that was meant to start fire! **Tansen was instructed to light the lamps by singing after Akbar, who was eager to see the miracle, ordered his slaves to set a number of them. **When Tansen sang Raga Deepak, all of the lamps simultaneously lit up!**
 
• Tansen also performed other miracles, such as bringing rain by singing Raga **Megh Malhar.** According to legend, **Tansen used this particular raga shortly after Raga Deepak.** This is due to the fact that Raga Deepak raised the temperature while Raga Megh Malhar lowered it. Raga Deepak has been lost to time, however Raga Megh Malhar is still in existence now.
 
• 
 
**Tansen was renowned for using music to communicate with animals.** A ferocious elephant is supposed to have once been brought into Akbar's court. All expectations were placed in Tansen because no one else could tame the animal. **The elephant was calmed by the emperor's favourite singer's songs**, and he also inspired Akbar to ride on it, which according to stories, Akbar did.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Raja Beerbal
 Birbal, or Raja Birbal, was a Saraswat Hindu Bhatt Brahmin advisor and main commander of the army in the court of the Mughal emperor, Akbar.
 
 

 Todar Mal
 Raja Todar Mal was the Finance Minister of the Mughal empire during Emperor Akbar's reign. He was also the Vakil-us-Sultanat and Joint Wazir
 
 

 Raja Man Singh
 Man Singh I, popularly known as Mirza Raja Man Singh was the 29th Kachwaha Rajput Raja of Amer, later known as Jaipur state, in Rajputana.

questions.question: Vernacular press Act was enacted in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Vernacular press act 1878**__

 __
 
• **​**__British India passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) to restrict press freedom and discourage criticism of British policy, notably the opposition that had risen since the commencement of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80).
 
• The Act was submitted by Lytton, the Viceroy of India at the time, and on March 14, 1878, the Viceroy's Council unanimously approved it. In order to "better control" the vernacular press and effectively penalise and prohibit "seditious literature" in "publications in oriental languages," the Vernacular Press Act (VPA) was passed.
 
• As a result, the British had nothing but hatred for the (non-English speaking) Indian press.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The** Bengal Gazette** was the first newspaper to be printed in India. **James Hickey**, the editor of this publication, was a vocal opponent of the East India Company. The newspaper was shut down as a result within two years of starting to publish.
 
• The Bengal Gazette served as the model for a number of Indian newspapers that are presently printed in all major languages. **These journals carried editorials that were anti-colonial and attacked the East India Company's haughtiness.**
 
• The existence of such columns was crucial in educating the rapidly emerging educated Indian class about the brutal colonial authority that had been imposed upon India by a force that professed to support democracy.
 
• **The East India Company, which wished to uphold its hegemony in India despite all obstacles, was harmed by this. **Especially when the Second Anglo-Afghan War began in 1878, newspapers like Amrita Bazar Patrika and others were vociferous in their condemnation of the British in India.
 
• **Viceroy Lord Lytton, therefore,** created the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 to regulate seditious reports in vernacular newspapers published in India in an effort to stop this.

 Due to the agitation, it produced among the Indians, Lord Ripon abolished the Vernacular Press Act in 1881.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a conductor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hand rubber.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 **Conductor__**

 __
 
• 
 
**​__**A substance or material that permits the flow of electricity is known as an electrical conductor. When voltage is provided, electrical charge carriers, often electrons or ions, travel effortlessly from atom to atom in a conductor.

 
 
• 
 
Several types of electrical conductors include - Human Body, Copper, Aluminium, Silver, Gold, Graphite, Platinum.

 
 
• 
 
Electric charges can easily pass through an electrical conductor. Conductivity is the ability of conductors to "conduct" electricity. Such materials provide less barrier to the movement of charges. Because electrons can freely flow through conducting materials, charge transfer is simple. Such materials offer less opposition or “resistance” to the flow of charges. Conducting materials allows easy charge transfer because of the free movement of electrons through them.

 
 
 
 
• **__Electrical Conductor Properties__**
 __
 
• 
 
The flow of electrons and ions via a conductor is constant.

 
 
• 
 
Since there is no electric field inside a conductor, electrons can move around freely.

 
 
• 
 
Inside a conductor, the charge density is zero.

 
 
• 
 
Free charges are only present on the conductor's surface.

 
 
• 
 
A conductor's points are all at the same potential.

 
 
• 
 
Many metals are effective electrical conductors. This is the rationale behind the use of metals in electrical appliance parts. Insulators are the plastic casings that shield electrical conductors. We won't experience an electric shock thanks to it.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Solid Conductor__
 
• Metallic Conductor: Silver, Copper, Aluminum, Gold, etc.
 
• Non-Metallic Conductor: Graphite
 
• Alloy Conductor: Brass, Bronze, etc.
 
• __**Liquid Conductor**__
 
• Metallic Conductor: Mercury
 
• Non Metallic Conductor: Saline Water, Acid Solution, etc.
 
• Copper Conductor is the most common material used for electrical wiring.
 
• Gold Conductor is used for high-quality surface-to-surface contacts.
 
• Silver is the best conductor on the Conductors list.
 
• Impure Water is listed in the Conductor List but it has less conductivity.

questions.question: Who among the following belonged to the ancient chiefly family of the Cholas from Uraiyur, captured the Kaveri delta from the Muttaraiyar in the middle of the ninth centuary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayalaya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Vijayalaya **____**​**__

 __
 
• The mediaeval** Chola kingdom was started** by Vijayalaya Chola, who gave it a solid foundation.
 
• He was one of those kings who built up an **empire from nothing, conquered strong neighbouring empires like the Pandyas and the Pallavas,** and rose to prominence throughout all of ancient South India.
 
• The early Cholas were extremely powerful, but they gradually lost it and were reduced to serving as feudal lords for other kingdoms. Around 300 A.D., they entered total darkness. Cholas vanished entirely from their homeland after this time. Around 848 A.D., **a hero of Chola **descent who we now know to as the great Vijayalaya Chola restored Chola authority.
 
• The name** Parakesarivarman** was given to him. He rebuilt the** Lord's Shiva temple in Narthamalai called Vijayalaya Choleeswaram which was built by Mutharayars.**
 
• **Varagunavarman II of the Pandyas and Nandivarman III of the Pallavas** came up with a strategy to stymie the Cholas' growing influence in South India after suffering a devastating loss at the hands of Vijayalaya Chola.
 
• First, Varagunavarman II mounted an army-sized incursion into Chola territory. The Pandyan army arrived at the Kaveri River's north bank. Vijayalaya was quite elderly and unable to participate in conflicts at this point.
 
• **Aditya I,** however, one of his sons, was also a renowned Chola emperor. In our articles titled "Battle Of Sri Purambiam" and "Aditya I," we fully explain what happened when his son seized command of the army. Vijayalaya's son took over command of the army after he died of aging, probably around 871 A.D. **and he was succeeded by his son Aditya I.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Gandaraditha Chola
 
 
Around 955 CE, Gandaraditha Chola succeeded his father Parantaka I to rule the Chola kingdom. He also wrote poetry in Tamil for the Thiruvisaippa Palandu. Madurantaka Chola, commonly known as Uttama Chola, one of his children, succeeded his cousin Sundara Chola as the Chola ruler.

 
 
 

 Parantaka Chola I
 Parantaka Chola I was a Chola emperor who ruled for forty-eight years. He conquered Rajasimhan II to acquire Pandya and defeated the Rashtrakutas in the Vallala war in the Deccan before 916 CE. His reign's most successful period was characterised by rising success and affluence.
 
 

 Aditya Chola I
 The Imperial Chola Empire was founded by Aditya Chola I (c. 870/71 - c. 907 CE), the son of Vijayalaya Chola, who overthrew the Pallavas and occupied the Western Ganga Kingdom. Aditya Chola I was succeeded by his eldest son Parantaka Chola I.

questions.question: In a food chain, secondary producers are _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "__Herbivores__".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a** food chain**, secondary producers are herbivores.
 
• **Herbivores** are those organisms that feed on trees, plants, and fruits.
 
• It is food for a predator.
 
• **Secondary producers** are also consumers.
 
• Most herbivores have wide flat teeth that help them to grind grass, tree parts, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Food chain - **It is an order of events occurring in the ecosystem, it shows one living organism eating another.
 
• **The food chain consists of :**
 
 
• Producers
 
• Primary consumers
 
• Secondary consumers
 
• Tertiary consumers
 
 
 
• **The producers**
 
 
• are the ones that produce food. 
 
• these include all the autotrophs, like phytoplankton, green plants, etc.
 
 
 
• **Consumers**
 
 
• these are dependent on other organisms or plants for food.
 
• includes herbivores, carnivores, etc.
 
 
 
• **Omnivores -** Organisms that eat both plants and animals.
 
• **Carnivores -** Organisms that eat animals.
 
• **Decomposers -** These feed on dead and decaying things.

__
 
• **Rabi crops** are those which are sown during winter and harvested in the spring season.
 
• These are sown around mid-November mostly after the monsoon is over and harvested in April or May.

• So, **Barley** is a Rabi crop in North India.​

• **There are three cropping seasons in India:**

 
 
• Kharif season
 
• Rabi season
 
• Zaid season
 
 
 
• **Kharif season -**
 
 
• This season starts in June and ends in October.
 
• The crops are sown in June and harvested in September.
 
• These include Rice, Sorghum, Maize, Tea, etc. 
 
 
 
• **Rabi season -**
 
 
• The crops are sown during October and harvested in February.
 
• These are winter-season crops.
 
• These include wheat, oats, barley, pulses, etc.
 
 
 
• **Zaid season -**
 
 
• These are sown in March and harvested in June.
 
• These include Seasonal fruits and vegetables.

questions.question: In the first phase of the green revolution, the use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent of which group of states?

options.text: Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh

• **HYVs** are High Yielding Variety of seeds that produces a large number of crops.

• In this era, farmers started using high-yielding varieties of cereals, the use of pesticides increased and other ways of irrigation were used.
